title: A Spectral Proof of the Hypergraph Moore Bound
abstract: A nonempty subfamily of a $k$-uniform hypergraph is an \emph{even cover} if every vertex lies in an even number of its hyperedges; for $k=2$ these are edge-disjoint unions of cycles, so the minimum size of an even cover is the natural hypergraph analogue of girth. We prove Feige's 2008 conjecture on the hypergraph Moore bound: there are absolute constants $A$ and $C$ (independent of $k$) such that for every $k\ge3$ and every $1\le\ell\le n$, any $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices with more than $C\,n^{k/2}/\ell^{k/2-1}$ hyperedges contains an even cover of size at most $A\,\ell\log(en/\ell)$. Our proof is based on sharp spectral bounds for Kikuchi matrices, which we expect to be of independent interest; we apply them to the refutation of random constraint satisfaction problems in a companion paper.
summary: This paper provides a rigorous spectral proof of the Hypergraph Moore Bound conjecture. It uses advanced linear algebra and graph theory tools—specifically analyzing weighted, memory-augmented graphs derived from hypergraphs—to relate the density of edges to the minimum size of an 'even cover.' The result establishes fundamental combinatorial bounds applicable across various dimensions.
main_problem: The paper aims to prove Feige's conjecture on the hypergraph Moore bound, establishing absolute constants for the size of an even cover in a $k$-uniform hypergraph.
main_result: It proves that any sufficiently dense $k$-uniform hypergraph must contain an even cover whose size is bounded by $A\ell\log(en/\ell)$, or alternatively, the number of hyperedges must be below a specific threshold dependent on $n, k,$ and $\ell$.
method: The proof employs advanced spectral graph theory techniques applied to specialized matrices (Kikuchi matrices) derived from lifting the hypergraph structure into a memory-augmented graph. It uses trace methods and walk counting arguments.
model_or_system: The mathematical model is an abstract $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$ on $n$ vertices, analyzed via its associated Kikuchi graph defined on an $\ell$-slice of the hypercube. The analysis involves constructing a 'lifted graph with memory' to track parity constraints.
key_observables: Minimum size of an even cover ($	ext{gev}(H)$), average degree ($ ar{d}$) of the associated Kikuchi graph, and spectral norms of derived operators ($K$ or $L$).
important_parameters: The uniformity $k$, number of vertices $n$, hierarchy level $\ell$, and parameters $A$ and $C$ defining the bounds.
main_assumptions: The proof relies on assuming no small even cover exists to derive spectral bounds, and it handles technical difficulties for odd vs. even uniformity using specific weighting schemes ($\delta_e$).
paper_structure: The paper develops the argument by first defining the problem via spectral analysis of the Kikuchi graph, then tackling the even and odd uniformity cases separately, establishing bounds on $ ar{d}$ based on the non-existence of small even covers, and finally combining these results to prove the main theorem.
why_interesting: While purely combinatorial/graph theoretical, the reliance on spectral methods (eigenvalues, walk counting) applied to structured matrices shares deep mathematical parallels with techniques used in quantum information theory for analyzing entanglement or graph properties via adjacency operators.
